checks.interpretation: Evaluate necessity and error recovery for the task. Avoid purchases, contact messages or account changes on live sites. Distinguish a blocked submission from a tested successful backend path.

checks.oldGuidelineTitle: Run Fewer, Simpler Queries As Possible
checks.probe: First inspect public task/API response patterns for a scoped hypothesis. For a database judgment request supplied query traces or inspect read-only ORM/query code and caching paths; count queries and repeated data under the same task.
checks.interpretation: Public network requests cannot establish database query counts or complexity. The agent can review this criterion, but without source/traces the backend conclusion remains cantTell rather than an inferred pass.

checks.oldGuidelineTitle: Choose A Sustainable Hosting Provider
checks.probe: Discover carbon.txt and public hosting/CDN evidence; record named providers, covered services, geographical/temporal boundaries and linked verification. Compare DNS/request evidence with the declarations and requested audience geography.
checks.interpretation: Self-published renewable claims do not prove energy procurement, matching or the actual served infrastructure. A CDN and local server are tradeoffs; deployment/source relationship and provider evidence must be scoped.

checks.oldGuidelineTitle: Optimize Browser Caching
checks.probe: Record response cache directives, validators and fresh/warm reload transfers using a declared cache state. Check an explicit offline task; distinguish private/dynamic responses from public assets and inspect supplied cache configuration.
checks.interpretation: Browser cache behavior cannot establish origin-side query caching. Avoid caching sensitive or time-critical data; a service worker file alone does not prove useful offline access.

checks.oldGuidelineTitle: Compress Your Files
checks.probe: Inspect successful text response Content-Encoding, encoded transfer and decoded size; account for HTTP/browser caching and partial capture. Compare representative text and already-compressed formats.
checks.interpretation: Compressible uncompressed responses are candidates; do not recompress every media type or equate a missing header on a cached/failed response with a demonstrated server issue.

checks.oldGuidelineTitle: Compress Your Files
checks.probe: Record media format, transfer KB, intrinsic/rendered dimensions, device pixel ratio, location relative to the viewport, loading/preload attributes and timing across initial/consent/scroll states. Exercise available controls and alternative delivery choices.
checks.interpretation: Judge media purpose and legibility before recommending removal, resizing or a codec. Modern formats and lazy attributes alone do not establish optimal delivery; instructional screenshots may need more detail than logos.

checks.oldGuidelineTitle: Use Error Pages And Redirects Carefully
checks.probe: Request one agreed missing path, inspect its HTTP status and content, then follow recovery navigation to complete the original task. Record bounded redirect chains for existing changed URLs if supplied.
checks.interpretation: A correct 404 status is not useful recovery by itself. Do not invent obsolete URLs to infer a redirect policy or crawl unlimited broken paths; distinguish intentional deletion from broken navigation.

checks.oldGuidelineTitle: Frequency For Refresh Is Relevant To Visitor Needs
checks.probe: Record request initiators, sizes, protocols and timing during task actions and a fixed idle interval; test explicit refresh/retry/cancel controls. Inspect supplied API/polling configuration for intended freshness constraints.
checks.interpretation: Polling or a protocol version alone is not a defect. Compare request frequency and payload with actual data freshness/user requirements; client timing cannot prove server processing efficiency.

checks.oldGuidelineTitle: Have An Ethical And Sustainability Product Strategy
checks.probe: Discover and read the relevant public statement and linked evidence. Record exact site/organization scope, accountable role, goals/baseline/time horizon, claimed actions, publication version and verification references; ask for missing implementation records when material.
checks.interpretation: A public document supports the existence/content of a commitment, not its execution. Evaluate scope and concrete commitments; lack of public evidence is not proof the organization has no practice.

checks.oldGuidelineTitle: Communicate The Ecological Impact Of User Choices
checks.probe: Capture exact impact statements, units, methodology, baseline, reporting period, traffic denominator and organizational boundaries; recompute published arithmetic and follow evidence references. Compare statements with audit observations only within matched scope.
checks.interpretation: Separate observed, modeled, estimated and verified claims. Public arithmetic can be checked, but operational/embodied/system boundaries and annual estimates need explicit assumptions; avoid implying certification.

checks.oldGuidelineTitle: Promote Responsible Data Practices
checks.probe: Read the privacy/data-ownership statement; identify controller, services/domains covered, purposes, retention and user controls. Compare the sampled consent/request behavior and optional source against those claims.
checks.interpretation: A policy for a related organization may not cover this origin. Surface ambiguity or contradiction with evidence; a sustainability audit is not a legal compliance determination.

checks.oldGuidelineTitle: Promote Responsible Emerging Technology Practices
checks.probe: Identify visible AI/emerging-technology features and disclosures, user alternatives and data collection. Request supplied model/provider settings, energy/impact rationale, evaluation records and mitigation ownership for a scoped review.
checks.interpretation: Public UI may not reveal AI use or its environmental cost. No visible feature is not proof of absence; distinguish observed behavior, declared governance and inaccessible operational evidence.
